story_type: sailboat rolling in a storm on a river bar, motor lifeboat tows it in
hook: Two sailors, lost in a storm, on a rough river bar.
narration: This sailboat was caught in a storm at the mouth of the Columbia River.
The two sailors aboard got disoriented and had trouble with their sails.
So they asked for help getting in across the Columbia River Bar.
A bar is where a river's current runs into ocean swells over shallow sand, and the waves stand up steep.
A forty seven foot motor lifeboat from Station Cape Disappointment came out for them.
The crew passed a tow line and pulled the sailboat in behind them.
Every swell rolled it hard onto its side.
outcome: The lifeboat crew towed the sailboat and both sailors across the rough bar.
title: Sailboat towed across a stormy bar
description:
On Nov. 7, 2015, a 47-foot Motor Life Boat crew from Coast Guard Station Cape Disappointment towed the disabled sailing vessel Turtle Dove across a rough Columbia River Bar after its two sailors were caught in a storm and asked for help.

Footage: U.S. Coast Guard video by Station Cape Disappointment, via DVIDS: https://www.dvidshub.net/video/434180/coast-guard-station-cape-disappointment-tows-sailing-vessel-across-columbia-river-bar
